messages.bing: I am a US beginner starting with no equipment. I need a complete setup to grind whole beans for espresso, brew espresso, and steam milk for two morning milk drinks, made sequentially. Integrated or separate equipment and manual or automatic milk preparation are acceptable. My hard limit is $800 for all required equipment combined, before tax and shipping; spending it is not a goal. Include necessary basic accessories or built-in equivalents, without automatically adding optional upgrades. Prioritize enjoyable, consistent drinks, approachable workflow, reasonable cleaning, dependable equipment, and seller confidence. Show your strongest complete options plus worthwhile less expensive alternatives and standalone machines or grinders that could contribute to a complete setup. I may combine compatible offers across providers. Return unchanged cards for every component you recommend purchasing. Explain meaningful benefits of paying more and identify material seller, variant, or functionality uncertainty. Distinguish the actual seller from a marketplace; ordinary missing accessory or voltage details need not disqualify credible US household offers. Prefer lower cost when expected satisfaction is essentially equal.

candidates.disclosure_and_withholding: Discloses the true combined ceiling, functional requirements, flexible configurations, and principal value criteria equally. Withholds no material purchasing constraint.
candidates.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Both providers may favor options near $800 and purchases contained within their own catalogs. Explicit requests for cheaper alternatives and useful individual components may broaden the returned choices, although neither provider is obliged to cooperate.
candidates.expected_user_value_tradeoff: Best chance of obtaining feasible, comparable complete setups while preserving opportunities to combine providers. Revealing the ceiling invites price anchoring, but prevents avoidable budget mismatches in this single round.

candidates.disclosure_and_withholding: Discloses the ceiling and core preferences to both. Requests different search emphases without claiming a private preference for either configuration.
candidates.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Bing may emphasize integrated purchases; Google may emphasize machine-and-grinder bundles. Both still have incentives to capture most of the budget and can return alternatives outside their assigned emphasis.
candidates.expected_user_value_tradeoff: May increase variety and complementary component coverage. However, unknown catalog strengths make specialization speculative, and it could suppress a provider's best offers despite the fallback requests.

candidates.disclosure_and_withholding: Discloses functional needs and value preferences but withholds the numerical budget from both providers without inventing a different ceiling.
candidates.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Providers may return broad price ranges, but their revenue incentives may favor expensive setups. They cannot reliably target the buyer's actual affordability boundary.
candidates.expected_user_value_tradeoff: Avoids explicitly anchoring recommendations at $800, but may leave too few feasible offers. With one round and omitted items unavailable, there is no opportunity to repair that gap.

selection_reason: Plan 1 provides both providers the information needed to return feasible offers and requests enough variety for independent comparison. With unknown catalogs and no follow-up round, this outweighs the potential benefits of specialization or budget secrecy.
limitations: No catalogs are visible, so product availability, prices, compatibility, and seller quality cannot be assessed.
Response forecasts are qualitative; revenue-seeking providers may omit valuable alternatives or emphasize favorable claims.
Only returned frozen cards will be available for the final purchase decision, which must still enforce the true complete-setup budget.
